name: Short SC.7 Skyvan
variants: SC.7 Skyvan Series 2 and 3 (Garrett TPE331 turboprops)
summary: Rugged, boxy British utility twin turboprop with twin fins and a rear cargo ramp; in the US it is almost entirely a skydiving jump ship.

wings: High, straight, strut-braced wing with a strut on each side
Wing tips are square and unswept
engines: Two turboprops in nacelles on the wing
fuselage: Extremely boxy, rectangular-section fuselage with a flat belly
Fixed landing gear in sponsons on the lower sides
Rear cargo ramp / door under the tail
tail: Twin fins and rudders on the ends of a boxy tailplane

tellTales: Slab-sided, rectangular fuselage with fixed wheels visible in side sponsons
Twin vertical fins on a boxy tailplane
High wing with a strut on each side and big, blunt engines

confusedWith.howToTell: The 330/360 has retracting landing gear and a longer, more modern fuselage; the Skyvan has fixed wheels in its sponsons and a blunt, shorter body (only the 330 shares its twin fins).
The C-212 has a single fin and an unbraced wing; the Skyvan has twin fins and strut-braced wings.
The Twin Otter has a single fin; the Skyvan has twin fins and a far boxier fuselage.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
